A 19th-century academic oil painting with a smooth, finely blended surface: soft glazed transitions, delicate fine detail, minimal visible brushstrokes, no heavy impasto, no rough texture. Strong light and shadow from a single warm source (a lamp, a torch, a fire, a low sun) or from heavy overcast, with deep chiaroscuro. Palette of umber, ochre, gold, olive and near-black, with occasional cool accents. The manner of a romantic landscape, a grand historical scene, or a natural-history study of a creature painted as if real. A low, close viewpoint. Wet, reflective stone where there is stone; ancient architecture where there is architecture; one saturated subject held against darkness; scale shown by something small beside something vast. Quiet, watchful, ominous mood. No text, no lettering, no border, no frame, no grid texture, not photographic.

A single figure standing on a low grassy rise at the edge of a high, flat, open plain, at first light on a cold, still morning in early spring, the hour before sunrise, seen from low in the wet grass a few paces behind it, looking north past it across the plain. Called the Chain or the Measure. A single human-seeming body. Tall and spare, built like a man who walks everywhere. Skin the grey of old iron. Eyes of dull copper. Hair cropped. A ridge of fine scale-like lines along the forearms, like survey marks. Stands very straight. The chain: a hundred equal links of one foot each, part of the body, carried and laid by hand. It is not a weapon. Clothes and gear, all ordinary: a long coat of undyed wool, plain and dark, with deep pockets, worn at the elbows and cuffs. A leather satchel on a cross strap, holding a small wooden mallet, a bundle of iron-shod stakes and a sack of chalk. A lead plumb bob on a waxed line. A folding rule of boxwood and brass. A hand-ruled tally book with a stub of pencil on a cord. One old, much-worn stake with notches down one side, kept in the inner pocket of the coat and not usually seen. Manner: patient and exact. Whistles when working something out. Not described by the player, and not to be invented: age of the face, voice, height in figures, anything of the senses. Seen from behind or in deep shadow, the head turned away or lost in darkness, no face visible. Here it has only this moment arrived: it stands still and very straight with its back to the viewer, the chain in one hand, the satchel on its shoulder, the hem of the coat dark with damp. The light is the cold grey of first light, with one low warm band of ochre and gold along the horizon at the right, where the sun has not yet risen; it catches the edge of the coat, the links of the chain and the wet turf of the rise, and everything else falls away toward near-black. Near the viewer: firm turf with last year's brown grass lying flat and new green coming through it, wet, and frost lying white in the hollows below the rise. In the middle distance the grassland runs flat and empty in every direction. To the right, about a mile off, an old paved road crosses the plain as a straight pale line. Ahead, about two miles off, a wide braided river runs in many channels between pale gravel bars, high and the color of clay, going away to the left. Ahead and to the right, about three miles off, one thin thread of smoke rises perfectly straight into the still air, with nothing visible at its foot. On the skyline ahead stands a long line of bare brown hills, and behind and above them a wall of very high snow mountains, cold and pale. Far away at the left edge of the skyline, very small and sharp, more snow peaks. No other figures, no animals, no buildings, no walls, no trees. The small upright figure against the wide plain and the snow heights gives the scale.
